stem: A 42-year-old woman presents to clinic with 8 weeks of bilateral symmetric polyarthritis affecting the metacarpophalangeal joints and wrists, with EXAM-CONFIRMED synovitis (boggy joint swelling, warmth, and tenderness on examination), morning stiffness lasting 90 minutes, and mild fatigue. Review of systems is OTHERWISE NEGATIVE: no malar rash, no oral ulcers, no Raynaud phenomenon, no sicca symptoms, no proteinuria or other renal symptoms, no cytopenias on CBC, no serositis, no preceding infection, no skin or nail psoriasis, no inflammatory bowel symptoms. Vital signs are normal. Labs DRAWN SO FAR: ESR 45 mm/h, CRP 18 mg/L (mildly elevated acute-phase reactants); CBC normal; basic metabolic panel normal; urinalysis bland; ANA 1:160 with a SPECKLED pattern (positive only on the limited panel ordered to date). Labs NOT YET DRAWN: rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP, anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, anti-U1-RNP, complement levels, hepatitis serology, parvovirus B19 serology. Hand and foot radiographs have NOT YET been performed.
question: Based on the information available, which is the most likely diagnosis?
rationale: Early rheumatoid arthritis is the most likely diagnosis. Exam-confirmed bilateral symmetric small-joint synovitis (MCPs and wrists), morning stiffness of 90 minutes, 8-week duration, and elevated acute-phase reactants form the classic early-RA picture; seronegative presentations are common at onset, so pending RF/anti-CCP does not displace RA as the leading diagnosis (2010 ACR/EULAR classification is completed, not replaced, by serology). The alternatives are disabled by documented negatives: SLE (B) requires additional clinical or immunologic domain points beyond arthritis — no rash, ulcers, serositis, cytopenia, or renal signs are present, and ANA 1:160 occurs in 5-30% of healthy adults; MCTD (C) requires high-titer anti-U1-RNP plus overlap features (Raynaud, sclerodactyly, myositis), all absent; UCTD (D) requires that the presentation not fit a defined CTD and typically >12 months of features, whereas this presentation fits early RA. Confirmatory workup (RF, anti-CCP, radiographs, ultrasound) refines but does not change the most likely diagnosis.

variants.stem_override: A 65-year-old postmenopausal woman presents to clinic with 8 weeks of bilateral symmetric polyarthritis (MCPs and wrists) with exam-confirmed synovitis, 90 minutes of morning stiffness, and mild fatigue. Review of systems is otherwise negative (no rash, no oral ulcers, no Raynaud, no sicca, no renal or hematologic symptoms, no preceding infection, no psoriasis, no IBD). ESR 45, CRP 18; CBC normal; urinalysis bland. ANA 1:160 speckled (positive on limited panel). RF, anti-CCP, anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, anti-Ro/La, anti-U1-RNP, complement levels, hepatitis serology, and parvovirus serology have NOT yet been drawn. Hand and foot radiographs have NOT yet been performed.
variants.rationale_for_variant: Age perturbation only — older age increases the pretest probability of every option in the differential (ANA prevalence rises with age — up to 25–30% in healthy adults >65; RA incidence peaks in the 60s; UCTD is increasingly recognized in older adults). However, the elevated pretest probability does NOT compensate for the missing information. The correct response remains to recognize the limits of the available data and complete the workup before committing to a diagnosis.

variants.stem_override: A 42-year-old woman presents to clinic with the same 8-week presentation of bilateral symmetric polyarthritis with exam-confirmed synovitis, 90 minutes of morning stiffness, mild fatigue, and an otherwise negative review of systems. ESR 45, CRP 18; CBC normal; urinalysis bland; ANA 1:160 speckled. The repeat serology workup has now returned with one additional result: anti-double-stranded DNA antibody at a LOW-TITER POSITIVE level (just above the assay cutoff). RF, anti-CCP, anti-Sm, anti-Ro/La, anti-U1-RNP, complement levels, and hepatitis/parvovirus serology are still pending. Hand and foot radiographs are still pending.
variants.rationale_for_variant: Mixed perturbation: a positive low-titer anti-dsDNA is added to the otherwise identical stem. This moves the correct answer from early RA (A) to SLE (B): with the ANA >=1:80 entry criterion met, the 2019 EULAR/ACR score reaches classification threshold (arthritis 6 + anti-dsDNA 6 = 12 >= 10), and anti-dsDNA is highly specific for SLE, whereas it is not a feature of RA. Tests whether the model updates the diagnosis on a single high-specificity immunologic finding.
